title: Arithmetic Operators
subtopics: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of arithmetic operators and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study arithmetic operators with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you predict calculations accurately and make conversion or precision trade-offs visible. In this lesson, focus on addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder with integer division before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder
items.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact.

items.title: Integer division
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: Division by zero behavior
items.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact.

items.title: Arithmetic with different numeric types
items.text: Operator precedence, numeric promotion, conversion, and overflow all affect results. Add parentheses when intent is not obvious and use a suitable decimal representation when exact base-10 arithmetic is required. Apply that reasoning specifically to arithmetic with different numeric types and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.

common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.
